01 / HOW IT STARTED
PERSONAL EXPERIENCE ≠ ACADEMIC EVIDENCE

That was my fan journey.
What happens when TikTok can initiate millions like it?

Hazard got my attention. Chelsea became my team. In between were the matches, the players, the culture and the feeling that this club somehow belonged to me.

An autobiographical illustration, not a finding.

→→→→→→
THE QUESTION BEHIND EVERYTHING

How does TikTok's personalized short-form content environment influence sports fan discovery, engagement, participation and brand loyalty?

Or, in normal-person language:

How does somebody go from “Who the hell is that?” to “That’s my team”?
02 / MORE THAN A SEAT

FANDOM HAS MORE
ADDRESSES NOW.

The stadium. The couch. The group chat. The feed. What does being a sports fan actually look like in 2026?

IN THE STANDS

THE SEAT

Showing up still matters. It is just no longer the only address fandom has.

IN THE FEED

THE SCREEN

Highlights, edits, creators and athletes can become the first point of contact.

TOGETHER, ELSEWHERE

THE GROUP CHAT

Debates, fantasy leagues, reactions and inside jokes turn spectators into participants.

Watch partiesFan editsFantasy leaguesHighlightsSecond screensAthlete merchandiseGroup chats

Photography and visual examples illustrate sports settings, not evidence of audience trends or media habits.

03 / THE PROPOSED FRAMEWORK

A VIEW IS JUST
THE OPENING WHISTLE.

Five connected stages. Plenty of detours. Click a stage to explore what might happen next.

01
FIRST CONTACT

DISCOVERY

Wait. Who is that?

First exposure to an athlete, team, league, sport, rivalry, storyline or piece of sports culture.

02
COME BACK

ENGAGEMENT

Okay, one more video.

Watching, rewatching, liking, commenting, sharing, following, searching and choosing another piece of related content.

03
JOIN IN

PARTICIPATION

I have thoughts.

Posting reactions, creating edits, joining debates, playing fantasy, sharing memes or contributing to the community around the sport.

04
BELONG

IDENTITY

That’s my team.

The shift from “I watch this” to “this is part of who I am.” Team language, rituals, symbols and group membership start to matter.

05
STICK AROUND

LOYALTY

Yes, even this season.

Continued attention and attachment over time, including the ugly seasons. Digital engagement can contribute to loyalty, but does not automatically create it.

A working conceptual model. Fans can skip stages, move backward or leave entirely.

JG’S TAKE · EDITORIAL COPY

Sports fans say “we won” after contributing absolutely nothing to the victory. That level of identification is exactly why fandom is fascinating.

01 / THE STADIUM

FANDOM
STILL LIVES
HERE.

Tickets, chants, rituals and shared physical experiences remain some of the strongest expressions of sports identity.

02 / THE FEED

THE NEW
FRONT DOOR.

A highlight, athlete clip or recommendation can introduce someone to a player or team before they ever watch a full game.

03 / THE GROUP CHAT

FANS DON'T
JUST WATCH.

Memes, fantasy, reactions, debates and fan-created content turn watching sports into something fans actively contribute to.

THE STADIUM DIDN'T DISAPPEAR. FANDOM JUST GOT MORE ADDRESSES.
JG’S TAKE

I found Chelsea through Eden Hazard. The next fan might find their Hazard while scrolling at 1:14 a.m. The entry point changed. The attachment can still become real.

05 / HOW FANDOM FOUND YOU

THEN VS. NOW

FamilyGeographyTelevisionLocal teamFavorite playerNewspaperSportsCenterFriendsGoing to games
For You PageAthlete clipsCreatorsHighlightsMemesAlgorithmsFantasy sportsGroup chatsFan editsBehind the scenesViral moments

What happens when geography is no longer the gatekeeper of fandom?

The point is not that TikTok replaced traditional fandom. It added another pathway into it.

THE $17 HOT DOG TEST

HOW FAR DID DIGITAL FANDOM
ACTUALLY TRAVEL?

SAW A VIDEO→WATCHED ANOTHER→FOLLOWED→COMMENTED→JOINED COMMUNITY→WATCHED A GAME→BOUGHT JERSEY→BOUGHT TICKET→PAID AN OFFENSIVE AMOUNT FOR STADIUM FOOD→STILL CAME BACK
JG’S TAKE

Getting 2 million views is cool. Getting somebody to willingly pay $17 for a stadium hot dog might tell us a little more.

John Gates is looking at sports fandom from four angles at once. The project is not a personal portfolio. Those perspectives are the reason this question matters to him.

He has spent much of his life around sports. Now he wants to understand how the next generation may arrive there differently.
